title: Coalescing eviction guardrails + stable snapshot certificates for batch-aware KV reclaim
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: continuous batching causes frequent concurrent accesses to KV prefix entries. When eviction runs while batches are in-flight, we see transient prefix-mismatch reads and rare correctness anomalies in long-running conversations. Current LRU/TTL heuristics reclaim memory eagerly and don't respect batch boundaries or GPU slab fragmentation, leading to increased tail latency and occasional regeneration of large KV footprints.

Proposal: introduce a lightweight guardrail layer that (1) pins prefix snapshots for the duration of in-flight batch epochs, (2) coalesces eviction operations to stable epoch boundaries, (3) adds a compact eviction certificate (a stable-snapshot ID + version) that readers can validate to guarantee prefix coherence, and (4) opportunistically reclaims GPU slabs using slab-aware heuristics to reduce fragmentation. The design aims to provide correctness guarantees without significantly raising memory pressure or latency for short-lived requests.
acceptance_criteria: No prefix-mismatch regressions in synthetic long-conversation replay tests (1000+ conversations, 95th/99th token-level correctness preserved)
End-to-end p99 token latency change <= +5% for steady workloads compared to baseline, under default batch config
GPU memory fragmentation reduced by >10% in mixed workloads (embedding+generation) versus naive LRU reclaim
Eviction certificate produced for every coalesced eviction window and validated by reader path; certificate validation logic covered by unit tests
Rollout plan and feature flag implemented for canary -> gradual release with telemetry to detect regressions
steps: Design: define epoch boundary semantics and snapshot lifetime relative to continuous-batching window
Implement snapshot pinning and fast-path reader certificate check in serving runtime
Add coalesced eviction scheduler that batches eviction candidates and executes at epoch boundaries
Integrate GPU slab-aware reclamation heuristics that prefer whole-slab frees to reduce fragmentation
Add metrics: snapshot_count, snapshot_pin_duration_ms, eviction_coalesce_window_ms, slab_reclaims, certificate_validation_failures
End-to-end tests: replay harness, randomized eviction/inflight-batch fuzzing, long-conversation correctness suite
Performance evaluation and canary rollout with feature flag and automatic rollback
decisions: Use epoch-based boundaries aligned with the continuous batching loop (not per-request), so evictions only occur between epochs
Eviction certificate will be a 64-bit snapshot ID + monotonic epoch counter (compact and cacheable)
Snapshots will be sticky only for active prefixes touched by in-flight batches; global pinning avoided to limit memory overhead
GPU reclamation will prefer freeing entire 256MB slabs where possible; partial frees will use a fast bitmap to mark free ranges
Default coalescing window set to 50ms, configurable via runtime flag; experiment with 25ms and 100ms in perf tests
open_risks: Increased short-term memory pressure for workloads with many concurrent long conversations if snapshots pin too many prefixes
Certificate validation adds a tiny cost on the hot path; risk of p99 latency increase if not optimized
Slab-aware reclamation requires allocator changes and could introduce subtle bugs on older GPU drivers
Rollback complexity: need fast disable path that drains snapshots without causing a flood of recomputations
